discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated matter with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and LMU Munich, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller and co-workers proposed in 1998 that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Hubbard model with tunable parameters. Greiner and Bloch then observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator quantum phase transition in 2002, turning a theorist's model into a laboratory system. The same groups later built quantum gas microscopes that image and control single atoms at single lattice sites. With these instruments, experiments have seen antiferromagnetic correlations, string order and many-body localisation in fermionic Hubbard systems, and have followed non-equilibrium dynamics that classical computers cannot model. The work founded analogue quantum simulation, which is now standard in laboratories worldwide. It links atomic physics to the central open problems of condensed matter, including high-temperature superconductivity and quantum magnetism, and it is the basis of today's neutral-atom quantum processors. The three nominees are responsible for its conception, its first demonstration and its single-site realisation.
